subject: Privacy pathways & onshore exception request — evidence and routing plan
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@healthco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@healthco.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Apr 2025 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: onshore exception + evidence for UK routing

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the call today. To move our compliance board forward we need a compact package showing:
- which subprocessors will ever touch EU customer data for our HealthCo tenant;
- any onshore-processing exceptions (UK-only) and planned mitigations;
- a proposed timeline to provide TIA / DTIA evidence and the SCCs/UK addendum redlines.

Can Redwood commit to a week-long evidence sprint (deliverables: subprocessor attestation, routing matrix, and redlines draft) so we can book our internal review on Apr 22? Also, please flag anything that requires enterprise legal review or an exception from our side.

Appreciate a clear owner and ETA.

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Head of Privacy Operations | HealthCo
(elena.park@healthco.com)

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@healthco.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 9 Apr 2025 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onshore exception + evidence for UK routing

Elena — thanks for the summary and the clear ask. We can run a focused sprint. High-level plan:

1) Sprint owners: Rishi (controls/evidence) + Jordan (routing/subprocessors).
2) Deliverables (ETA Apr 16): subprocessor_attestation.pdf, proposed_routing_matrix.csv, and a first-pass uk-addendum-redlines.docx.
3) Blockers: any legal redlines that deviate from our standard UK IDTA will need counsel review (we'll surface).

I'll coordinate a short intake later today to confirm the exact subprocessor list you want in the attestation (full list vs. in-scope only). If HealthCo can share the preferred template for attestations it will speed us up — otherwise we will use our standard format.

Action items from us: assign sprint backlog, run evidence collection, and route the redlines to our legal. Will that timeline work for your Apr 22 review?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: proposed_routing_matrix.csv (stub)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@healthco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@counselpartners.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Apr 2025 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onshore exception + evidence for UK routing

Thanks — quick clarifications from our side so the evidence sprint is scoped correctly:

- Scope for attestation: we'll include all active subprocessors that have technical or logical access to customer data for HealthCo (i.e., inference serving, embeddings, logging/retention stores). If you want us to exclude internal monitoring-only agents, please confirm.
- Onshore exception: we're proposing a conditional UK-only onshore path for PII derived from UK-resident subjects. This will be enforced by routing flags at the tenant layer and a hardened KV cache that does not leave UK-hosted nodes. We will document fallback behavior (route to EU if capacity shortfall).
- SCCs / UK Addendum: attached is a first-pass redline (uk-addendum-redlines.docx). Counsel Tom — can you weigh in on the data localization phrasing?

Tentative ETA remains Apr 16 for the deliverables. If HealthCo needs encryption-in-transit proofs or HSM/KMS key origin details we can add a short appendix.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Controls | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor_attestation.pdf (draft), uk-addendum-redlines.docx (draft)

Date: Fri, 11 Apr 2025 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: onshore exception + evidence for UK routing

Marissa / Rishi — this looks great, thanks for the quick turnaround and the drafts. A few notes from our reviewers: 

- Attestation: HealthCo requires a signed attestation (pdf) listing subprocessors + access types. The draft looks good but please add a column for "data categories" (PII / inferred health signal / anonymized telemetry).
- Routing matrix: please call out fallback behavior explicitly when UK capacity is constrained — state the SLA we should expect (e.g., 99th percentile latency bump).
- UK addendum redlines: Counsel flagged the phrase "onshore processing" as ambiguous. Tom (cc'd) suggests explicit language about KMS key locality and whether logs are replicated out of region.

Tom — if you could share two quick suggested edits on the addendum we can close legal review.

If you can provide the updated attestation and matrix by Apr 16 EOD we'll lock the April 22 compliance board. Also please include a one-page executive summary (single page) for our board packet.

Thanks,
Elena
